result.title: Paired-Outcome Learning for Selective Spacecraft Attitude Capture under Torque Limits
result.summary: Torque-limited spacecraft attitude capture requires adapting the maneuver speed to uncertain braking authority. Faster settings can reduce average tracking error while worsening individual maneuvers, making selective modification of an existing controller a baseline-relative learning problem. A paired-outcome method combines three mechanisms: physically interpretable continuation policies with different speed envelopes, separate prediction of task failure and successful-pair tracking gains, and context-dependent rejection that executes the unchanged baseline. Complete paired simulations provide labels under common plant parameters and measurement seeds; training, validation, and calibration are separated by context. Basilisk experiments use 108 development contexts, 324 labeling rollouts, and 624 evaluation episodes across 48 test contexts, including disclosed post-freeze diagnostics. The selective controller reduces aggregate integrated attitude error by 4.67% relative to the branch baseline, with 17 improvements, 31 exact ties, and no observed regressions. Always using the fast alternative achieves a 4.81% reduction but worsens 11 cases. Gains occur in principal-axis, near-axis, braking-boundary, and selected noise/drift maneuvers; general coupled cases retain the baseline. Ablations show no additional aggregate benefit from branch commitment, active querying, or score subtraction. The evidence supports a restricted empirical trade-off between average improvement and individual regression, without establishing a closed-loop safety guarantee.

AI.brief_summary: 论文研究力矩受限下航天器姿态捕获控制器的选择性改造：用 paired-outcome 方法对同一上下文下的「失败」与「成功配对增益」分别预测，并在收益不确定时回退执行原始基线控制器，从而在平均收益与单次退化之间取舍。
AI.relevance_reason: 其「成对结果监督 + 上下文相关拒绝并回退基线」的机制，可能为 LVR 中何时启用高成本 latent 推理、如何抑制个别样本退化提供可核查的方法线索，但与视觉或多模态推理无直接关联。
